summary: The Investing in All of America Act of 2025 modifies how Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs) are funded and regulated by the Small Business Administration. It adjusts the maximum financing limits available to SBICs, expands what counts as private capital by including college and university endowments or trusts, and excludes certain investments—such as those in rural areas, critical technology fields, and small manufacturers—from standard financing calculations.

affected_groups.effect: Face new general financing limits, expanded definitions of private capital, and new exclusions for specific types of investments.
May receive targeted investments that are excluded from standard SBIC financing limit calculations.
affected_groups.group: Small businesses in rural areas, critical technology categories, and small manufacturers

affected_groups.effect: Can now have their funds officially considered part of an SBIC's private capital.
affected_groups.group: College and university trusts and endowments

key_provisions: Reduces the maximum general outstanding financing available to an SBIC from 300% to 200% of its private capital.
Increases the maximum financing cap from $350 million to $475 million for two or more commonly controlled SBICs that make quarterly or semiannual interest payments.
Expands the definition of an SBIC's private capital to include funds invested by the foundation, endowment, or trust of any college or university.
Excludes amounts invested in rural areas, critical technology categories, and small manufacturers from the calculation of the financing limit.
Caps the total excluded investment amounts at the lesser of 50% of the SBIC's private capital or $125 million.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Investing in All of America Act of 2025 modifies how Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs) are funded and regulated by the Small Business Administration. It adjusts the maximum financing limits available to SBICs, expands what counts as private capital by including college and university endowments or trusts, and excludes certain investments—such as those in rural areas, critical technology fields, and small manufacturers—from standard financing calculations.
summary_detail.significance: This law alters the financing boundaries and investment incentives for Small Business Investment Companies, directing special focus toward rural enterprises, small manufacturers, and critical technology sectors while altering how overall leverage caps are managed.
